realityChecks.title: The Bell-Hour Census
realityChecks.description: The 3-km radius carries a schools premium of ₹1,500–2,200/sqft — but it cliffs at the 12–15 minute drive line, not at a distance. The 11-minute community at ₹2,400/sqft less was the actual find.

realityChecks.title: The Swap, Not Double Exposure
realityChecks.description: Selling and buying in the same market is a hedge — the same repricing that inflated the target inflated the Koramangala exit. Once seen as a swap, the vertigo stopped.

realityChecks.title: The ₹30L Proximity Premium
realityChecks.description: ₹30L for one institution whose relationship with the child has eleven years of unknowns — computed, contested at dinner, and paid with a written list of what would have to go wrong.

realityChecks.title: The Chain Choreography
realityChecks.description: The buyer's delay and the seller's impatience collided for two weeks — resolved by trading price certainty for time: firm price, longer close, no theatrics.

realityChecks.title: The Life-Beyond-the-Gate Test
realityChecks.description: The school counselor's answer to 'what do families regret': buying for the school and forgetting the child changes — the clubhouse and park got re-weighted that evening.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “School-anchored families shop with a stopwatch at 7:50 am, and theirs was the cleanest version I've seen. The premium they paid wasn't for the school — it was for the 12-minute bell-hour line, and the census proved the cliff sits at time, not distance: the 11-minute community at ₹2,400/sqft less was the real find. Their best diligence was counting uniform stickers in a parking lot, and their hardest honesty was the second-child question, left open in the file. When the chain wobbled, they didn't panic — they traded price certainty for time, because they'd already learned the swap lesson: selling and buying in one market is a hedge, not a double exposure.”
